newsitem.title: UK: UK's FTSE 100 listless, but creeps back from lows.
newsitem.headline: UK's FTSE 100 listless, but creeps back from lows.

text.p: The UK's FTSE 100 index had nudged back into positive territory tracking a rebound in the futures market late Monday morning, but trade remained thin and listless with little else to help set direction.
The UK's blue-chip index was up a meagre 0.1 point at 4,851.6 by 1003 GMT although advancers outpaced decliners one-and-a-half times.
Mid-250 stocks were stuck in the doldrums to be down 6.2 at 4,468.5.
In the absense of any major scheduled corporate or economic news, the market lacked direction and was led by futures.
The lead index rebounded from lows of around 4,835, tracking a muted recovery in the futures market.

U.S. blue chips had limped slightly lower on Friday and failed to provide any direction. The Dow was expected to open flat to lower on Monday as nerves build up ahead of the key U.S. employment report on Friday.
Most investors in London seemed happy to sit back and wait for the flurry of major company earnings due later in the week and were wary that current valuations may be overstretched and unsustainable.

"There are more and more people trying to call the top of this market," said one equity salesman. "That is why this week is critical for London, because if the results are not up to scratch London has to think on what basis it will value itself."
Banking group Abbey National kicks off the half-year reporting season on Tuesday.

"We have one of our biggest weeks for results this week," said one dealer. "We're going to have to wait and see what comes out from these banking numbers because when you have such a narrow base to this rally in London you have to make sure that those companies are holding up alright."
